front.title: Enhanced Dual Stack: Connection-Informed IPv6/IPv4 Selection

abstract.t: This document describes Enhanced Dual Stack (EDS), a framework intended to reduce the operational risk and upfront workload of introducing IPv6 into existing IPv4 networks. EDS provides a connection-informed method for implementing RFC 6724 Rule 1, "Avoid unusable destinations", by remembering recent TCP/QUIC connection- establishment failures and avoiding repeated selection of affected IPv6 destinations. It also provides operational diagnostics so administrators can identify and correct IPv6 problems. EDS is complementary to Happy Eyeballs and does not require connection racing. By starting with selected EDS-capable pioneer hosts, performing practical validation, and expanding IPv6 gradually, EDS can be deployed incrementally without requiring all hosts to support EDS. With EDS, enterprises' IPv6 introduction can change from a heavy upfront validation process toward an incremental improvement process.
